This table shows the number of civilians employed by the U.S. government each year from 1915 to 1918.

Number of Civilians Employed by the Federal Government, 1915–1918

| Year | Total   |
|------|---------|
| 1915 | 395,429 |
| 1916 | 399,881 |
| 1917 | 438,500 |
| 1918 | 854,500 |

Based on this table, how did World War I affect the U.S. economy?

options.label: F
options.text: It led to decreased spending in order to conserve resources during the war effort.

options.label: G
options.text: It led to decreased pressure on private companies to supply the war effort.

options.label: H
options.text: It increased the economic opportunities available for U.S. citizens.

options.label: J
options.text: It increased the number of immigrants searching for U.S. jobs.
